newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean polyethylene shares up on Japan fire news.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean polyethylene shares up on Japan fire news.

text.p: Shares of Daelim Industrial Co and other South Korean polyethylene makers rose in late Friday trading on hopes that their earnings would benefit from a fire at a Japanese polyethylene plant, brokers said.
Daelim rose 540 won to 8,600 won, Hanwha Chemical Corp by 410 won to 8,710 and Honam Petrochemical Co by 800 won to 14,500.
A polyethylene plant owned jointly by DuPont Co and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd in western Japan was shut down after a fire broke out early Friday, a spokesman for the joint venture said.
The fire was brought under control after about 15 minutes, but the spokesman said it was unclear when the plant could resume operations.
"The news immediately boosted buying orders," said analyst Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
"I'm not sure how long and how much the impact will last in the market as we have to see more details."
